fw-poetics.title: Aristotle, Poetics (S. H. Butcher translation)
fw-poetics.notes: Action, characterization, recognition and causal plot; a historical theory, not universal law.

fw-leguin.title: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Carrier Bag Theory of Fiction (publisher overview)
fw-leguin.notes: Alternative narrative structures and value systems. Dated 1986, first published in Women of Vision (1988), collected in Dancing at the Edge of the World (1989). Official page is an overview, not full text.

fw-forster.title: E. M. Forster, Aspects of the Novel (1927), primary text
fw-forster.notes: Verified original book text; chapter distinctions between story, character and plot. Project Gutenberg digital release date is not the original book date.

fw-worldbuilding.title: Worldbuilding: literary and fictional-setting practice (overview)
fw-worldbuilding.notes: General overview used for terminology, not a claim that a specific method is empirically validated.

fw-perspective.title: Perspective — Point of View, The Living Handbook of Narratology
fw-perspective.notes: Scholarly overview of voice versus focalization, focalization types, and point of view. Terminology from narrative theory, not a mandatory craft recipe.

fw-unreliability.title: Dan Shen, Unreliability, The Living Handbook of Narratology
fw-unreliability.notes: Scholarly account distinguishing failures of reporting, interpreting, and evaluating; discussion of Booth and subsequent classifications.

fw-forster-text.title: E. M. Forster, Aspects of the Novel (1927), full-text edition
fw-forster-text.notes: Primary text for the contrast between story chronology and plot causality; not a claim that one type of fiction is universally superior.

fw-modern-iowa.title: Iowa Writers Workshop: Our History
fw-modern-iowa.notes: Founding in 1936 and the development of workshops; not evidence for a single mandatory aesthetic.

fw-modern-programera.title: Mark McGurl, The Program Era: Postwar Fiction and the Rise of Creative Writing (2009)
fw-modern-programera.notes: Institutional impact of creative writing programs on postwar American fiction.

fw-modern-salesses.title: Matthew Salesses, Craft in the Real World: Rethinking Fiction Writing and Workshopping (2021)
fw-modern-salesses.notes: Challenges naturalized workshop values and asks about cultural expectations and voice.

fw-modern-saunders.title: George Saunders, A Swim in a Pond in the Rain (2021)
fw-modern-saunders.notes: Craft teaching through detailed analysis of readerly experience in short fiction.

fw-modern-carver.title: Raymond Carver, handbook chapter, De Gruyter (2022)
fw-modern-carver.notes: Carver minimalism and Lish editorial context; Carver did not originate minimalism.

fw-modern-lish.title: The Poetics of the Sentence: Gordon Lish Literary Legacy (2015)
fw-modern-lish.notes: Lish editorial role in some American minimalist and dirty-realist work.

fw-modern-maximalism.title: Stefano Ercolino, The Maximalist Novel (2014)
fw-modern-maximalism.notes: Scholar proposed characteristics of maximalist novels; a critical taxonomy, not writers own manifesto.

fw-modern-barth.title: John Barth, The Literature of Exhaustion (1967), reprinted in Postmodernism and the Contemporary Novel
fw-modern-barth.notes: Barth discussion of exhausted possibilities; not a claim that fiction has ended.

fw-modern-postmodern-reader.title: Postmodernism and the Contemporary Novel: A Reader
fw-modern-postmodern-reader.notes: Historical context for fiction debates in the 1960s and 1970s.

fw-modern-oulipo.title: Dennis Duncan, The Oulipo and Modern Thought (2019)
fw-modern-oulipo.notes: History and implications of Oulipo and literary constraints.

fw-modern-oulipo-poetry.title: Poetry Foundation glossary, OuLiPo
fw-modern-oulipo-poetry.notes: Oulipo founding 1960 and exemplary procedural methods.

fw-modern-lanser.title: Susan Sniader Lanser, Fictions of Authority: Women Writers and Narrative Voice (1992)
fw-modern-lanser.notes: Feminist narratology and forms of narrative authority.

fw-modern-leguin-carrier.title: Ursula K Le Guin, The Carrier Bag Theory of Fiction (original 1980s essay)
fw-modern-leguin-carrier.notes: Alternative to hero-centered narrative. Dated 1986; first published 1988 in Women of Vision; 1989 collection. Official page is a summary.

fw-modern-leguin-craft.title: Ursula K Le Guin, Steering the Craft (1998; revised 2015)
fw-modern-leguin-craft.notes: Narrative language, syntax, viewpoint, and collective workshop practice.

fw-modern-truby.title: John Truby, The Anatomy of Story (2007)
fw-modern-truby.notes: Author-specific 22-step story design focused on character, plot and moral argument.

fw-modern-brody.title: Jessica Brody, Save the Cat! Writes a Novel (2018)
fw-modern-brody.notes: 15-beat screenplay adaptation to novels; the universal-beats claim is an authors method assertion.

fw-modern-storygrid.title: Shawn Coyne, The Story Grid (2015): publisher history

fw-modern-autofiction.title: Hywel Dix, Autofiction, Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Literature (2022)
fw-modern-autofiction.notes: Origins of the term and unsettled generic identity.

fw-modern-sincerity.title: Adam Kelly, New Sincerity: American Fiction in the Neoliberal Age (2024)
fw-modern-sincerity.notes: Interpretative account of late postmodern American fiction; not a general recipe.

fw-modern-climate.title: Matt Bell, Climate Fictions: Future-Making Technologies (2021)
fw-modern-climate.notes: Climate fiction as broad and overlapping with speculative modes.

fw-modern-pratt-afrofuturism.title: Pratt Institute Libraries, Afrofuturism research guide
fw-modern-pratt-afrofuturism.notes: Historical coinage, prior cultural histories and evolving practices.

fw-modern-indigenous.title: Grace L Dillon (ed), Walking the Clouds: An Anthology of Indigenous Science Fiction (2012)
fw-modern-indigenous.notes: Indigenous science fiction forms and editorial framing.

fw-modern-speculative.title: Speculative Fiction, Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Literature
fw-modern-speculative.notes: Contested definition and history of speculative fiction.

fw-modern-montfort.title: Nick Montfort, Twisty Little Passages: An Approach to Interactive Fiction (2003)
fw-modern-montfort.notes: Parser-based IF history and its relation to literary art and games.

fw-modern-rettberg.title: Jill Walker Rettberg, Hypertext Fiction from 1987 to 1999 (2010)
fw-modern-rettberg.notes: Hypertext fiction community and Storyspace history distinct from text games.

fw-modern-twine.title: Twine, open-source interactive-narrative project
fw-modern-twine.notes: Twine nonlinear HTML story tooling, choices, passages and variables.

fw-modern-modernism.title: Poetry Foundation glossary, Modernism
fw-modern-modernism.notes: Broad cultural historical context and formal experiments in early twentieth-century fiction; no claim of one homogeneous movement.

fw-modern-magical-realism.title: Michael Bell, Garcia Marquez, magical realism and world literature (2010)
fw-modern-magical-realism.notes: Cautions against simplified versions of magical realism and the Latin American Boom; One Hundred Years of Solitude published in 1967.

fw-hist-modernism-britishlibrary.title: British Library, Cities in modernist literature
fw-hist-modernism-britishlibrary.notes: Woolf, Mrs Dalloway and city, shared public time and divergent private consciousness.

fw-hist-modernism-cambridge.title: Pericles Lewis, The Cambridge Introduction to Modernism, prose fiction (2007)
fw-hist-modernism-cambridge.notes: Joyce and Woolf, experiment in time, interior monologue and narrative technique; avoids equating Ulysses with one stream of consciousness.

fw-hist-modernism-humphrey.title: Robert Humphrey, Stream of Consciousness in the Modern Novel (1954)
fw-hist-modernism-humphrey.notes: Distinguishes approaches to fictional consciousness in Richardson, Joyce, Woolf, Faulkner.

fw-hist-boom-oxford.title: Juan E. De Castro, The Latin American Novel in the 1960s and Early 1970s: The Boom and Beyond
fw-hist-boom-oxford.notes: Boom authors, antecedents, noncanonical writers and political/publishing setting.

fw-hist-boom-cambridge.title: Consuelo Saizar, Constructing Hegemony: Latin American Boom and Spain/Mexico book industries (2020)
fw-hist-boom-cambridge.notes: Boom as literary and publishing phenomenon mediated by Barcelona, agents and global networks.

fw-hist-boom-agent.title: Dominique Lear, Carmen Balcells: The Agent of the Latin American Literary Boom (2024)
fw-hist-boom-agent.notes: Balcells literary agency and role of gender, economic capital and transnational gatekeeping.

fw-hist-boom-coldwar.title: Deborah Cohn, The Latin American Literary Boom and U.S. Nationalism during the Cold War (2012)
fw-hist-boom-coldwar.notes: Cultural exchange networks, universities, publishers and Cold War relationships.

fw-hist-postcolonial-ngugi.title: Ngugi wa Thiong'o, Decolonising the Mind: The Politics of Language in African Literature (1986)
fw-hist-postcolonial-ngugi.notes: Argument for writing and cultural continuity in African languages; dates and contents.

fw-hist-postcolonial-achebe.title: Simon Gikandi, Between Realism and Modernism: Chinua Achebe and the Making of African Literature
fw-hist-postcolonial-achebe.notes: Achebe on reshaping English for African self-fashioning and literature.

fw-hist-postcolonial-language.title: English and/in Africa: reflections on the language question (2024)
fw-hist-postcolonial-language.notes: Critically compares Achebe/Ngugi and highlights additional positions.

fw-hist-postcolonial-rhys.title: Cora Kaplan, The Empire at Home: Jean Rhys and Wide Sargasso Sea
fw-hist-postcolonial-rhys.notes: Rhys 1966 novel reworks Jane Eyre from displaced and colonial subjectivities.

fw-hist-postcolonial-rushdie.title: The Cambridge Introduction to the Novel: Salman Rushdie, Midnight's Children (1981)
fw-hist-postcolonial-rushdie.notes: National independence history and expansive self-questioning narration.

fw-hist-publishing-goldstone.title: Andrew Goldstone, Origins of the US Genre-Fiction System, 1890-1956 (2023)
fw-hist-publishing-goldstone.notes: Genre categories institutionalized via pulps, then paperbacks; prestige stratification.

fw-hist-publishing-loc.title: Library of Congress, Pulp Fiction Collection
fw-hist-publishing-loc.notes: Pulp categories, production, pay and circulation 1920s-1950s.

fw-hist-publishing-program.title: University of Iowa Libraries, The Program Era Project
fw-hist-publishing-program.notes: Historical documentation of institutional creative writing training.

fw-hist-publishing-king.title: Angela S. Allan, Stephen King, Incorporated (2021)
fw-hist-publishing-king.notes: Genre authorship and shifts in corporate publishing economics.

fw-hist-publishing-kdp.title: Amazon, A look back at 10 years of the Amazon Kindle
fw-hist-publishing-kdp.notes: Company account of Kindle and self-publication launch in November 2007; do not treat marketing claims as independent outcome evidence.

fw-debate-leguin-carrier.title: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Carrier Bag Theory of Fiction (dated 1986; first published 1988; collected 1989)
fw-debate-leguin-carrier.notes: Author essay; Le Guin dates text 1986, Women of Vision publication is 1988, and collection Dancing at the Edge of the World is 1989. Official author site describes ideas, not the full 1988 publication record.

fw-debate-leguin-steering.title: Ursula K. Le Guin, Navigating the Ocean of Story: discussion of conflict and Steering the Craft
fw-debate-leguin-steering.notes: Author directly rejects reduction of all story to conflict and names alternative engines of change.

fw-debate-gardner-edelstein.title: Marilyn Edelstein, Ethics and Contemporary American Literature: Revisiting the Controversy over John Gardner (1996)
fw-debate-gardner-edelstein.notes: Documents 1978 controversy and takes moral argument seriously without accepting universal aesthetic verdicts.

fw-debate-gardner-review.title: Kirkus Reviews, On Moral Fiction (1978)
fw-debate-gardner-review.notes: Describes arguments and limitations of Gardner's 1978 intervention.

fw-debate-gardner-art.title: Kirkus Reviews, The Art of Fiction
fw-debate-gardner-art.notes: Summarizes Gardner's craft concepts of vivid continuous dream and profluence, separate from the 1978 polemic.

fw-debate-barth-exhaustion.title: Johns Hopkins University Libraries, John Barth: Exhaustion and Other Essays
fw-debate-barth-exhaustion.notes: Distinguishes exhausted artistic possibilities from art itself; discusses later replenishment essay.

fw-debate-barth-funhouse.title: Johns Hopkins University Libraries, Lost and Found in the Funhouse: Introduction
fw-debate-barth-funhouse.notes: Describes Ambrose, story/self-commentary, and narrative form.

fw-debate-barth-history.title: Johns Hopkins University Libraries, John Barth publication history
fw-debate-barth-history.notes: Dates major works and situates literary experimentation within a larger career.

fw-debate-saunders-book.title: Penguin Random House, A Swim in a Pond in the Rain by George Saunders (2021)
fw-debate-saunders-book.notes: Publisher description and publication date for seven Russian stories and close readings.

fw-debate-saunders-believer.title: The Believer, Interview with George Saunders (2021)
fw-debate-saunders-believer.notes: Saunders distinguishes close reading from universal prescriptions and discusses workshop revision.

fw-debate-saunders-harvard.title: The Harvard Advocate, Interview with George Saunders (2021)
fw-debate-saunders-harvard.notes: Saunders discusses course and moral ambiguity in Russian stories.

fw-debate-saunders-mayday.title: Mayday, George Saunders on A Swim in a Pond in the Rain (2021)
fw-debate-saunders-mayday.notes: Saunders discusses revision, curiosity, and story as a reader-oriented exchange.

fw-debate-saunders-esquire.title: Esquire, George Saunders on Liberation Day (2022)
fw-debate-saunders-esquire.notes: Reflective comments about experimentation, revision, ambiguity and surprise.

fw-compare-snyder-beats.title: Save the Cat!, Blake Snyder Beat Sheet: A Bridge to Story
fw-compare-snyder-beats.notes: First-party defense of structural beat-sheet methods; account of advocated approach, not independent validation.

fw-compare-gardner-reception.title: Robert Towers, Good Grief!, New York Review of Books (1978)
fw-compare-gardner-reception.notes: Contemporary critical review of Gardner On Moral Fiction and contested moral judgments.

fw-compare-barth-reference.title: John Barth, Oxford literature reference overview
fw-compare-barth-reference.notes: Dates and scope of Barth exhaustion/replenishment essays and postmodern techniques.

fw-compare-saunders-method.title: George Saunders, Office Hours: My (Approximate) Method (2024)
fw-compare-saunders-method.notes: Author stresses reader assessment and explicitly cautions against strict loyalty to a process.

fw-compare-saunders-limits.title: George Saunders, Method, Shmethod (2022)
fw-compare-saunders-limits.notes: Author directly qualifies his claims about revision methods.

fw-modern-carver-archive.title: William L. Stull and Maureen P. Carroll, Library of America Note on the Texts: Beginners and What We Talk About When We Talk About Love (2009)
fw-modern-carver-archive.notes: Editors document specific 1981 Lish cuts and 2009 restoration of manuscript versions. Evidence is collection-specific; not a blanket attribution of all Carver style to Lish.

fw-le-guin-1988.title: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Carrier Bag Theory of Fiction, in Women of Vision (St. Martin's Press, 1988)
fw-le-guin-1988.notes: Confirms first 1988 anthology appearance; distinguishes writing date 1986 from book-collection publication 1989.

fw-gardner-art-1984.title: John Gardner, The Art of Fiction: Notes on Craft for Young Writers, first book edition (Alfred A. Knopf, 1984)
fw-gardner-art-1984.notes: Catalogs the first book edition as 1984. Contemporary Kirkus review carries a 1983 date; do not conflate review and edition dates.

fw-leguin-always-coming-home.title: Ursula K. Le Guin, Always Coming Home (1985), official author work page
fw-leguin-always-coming-home.notes: Extended invented ethnography; example for worldbuilding and institution/culture analysis, not an empirical worldbuilding methodology.

fw-minds-cohn.title: Dorrit Cohn, Transparent Minds: Narrative Modes for Presenting Consciousness in Fiction (1978)
fw-minds-cohn.notes: Primary scholarly taxonomy: psycho-narration, quoted monologue, narrated monologue; date and scope established.

fw-minds-wood.title: James Wood, How Fiction Works (2008; tenth anniversary edition 2018)
fw-minds-wood.notes: Free indirect style, fictional perception, narrator and character styles; distinguish original from revised edition.

fw-minds-smith.title: Zadie Smith, Two Paths for the Novel (2008)
fw-minds-smith.notes: Compares Joseph O'Neill Netherland and Tom McCarthy Remainder; critique of a dominant lyrical realism rather than all realism.

fw-sincerity-wallace.title: David Foster Wallace, E Unibus Pluram: Television and U.S. Fiction (1993)
fw-sincerity-wallace.notes: Published The Review of Contemporary Fiction 13.2 (summer 1993); irony, television, and self-conscious literary forms.

fw-sincerity-kelly.title: Adam Kelly, David Foster Wallace and the New Sincerity in American Fiction (2010)
fw-sincerity-kelly.notes: Kelly's scholarly account appears in Consider David Foster Wallace: Critical Essays (2010); not a universal name for all later fiction.

fw-sincerity-scholars.title: Theo Savvas and Christopher K. Coffman, American Fiction after Postmodernism (2019)
fw-sincerity-scholars.notes: Reviews Wallace's 1993 argument and later post-postmodern/new sincerity scholarship; chronology and contested categories.

fw-autofiction-lejeune.title: Philippe Lejeune, Le Pacte autobiographique (1975), discussed in The Fictional in Autofiction
fw-autofiction-lejeune.notes: Lejeune's autobiography pact and author/narrator/protagonist naming logic; indirect modern scholarly discussion.

fw-autofiction-doubrovsky.title: Fiction in the Post-Truth Era: The Ironic Effects of Autofiction (2017)
fw-autofiction-doubrovsky.notes: Documents Doubrovsky coining autofiction in 1977 for Fils and later variation in definitions and publishing usage.

fw-autofiction-memory.title: On Autofiction and Cultural Memory (2024)
fw-autofiction-memory.notes: Surveys evolution of autofiction from Lejeune/Doubrovsky and its relation to memory and cultural framing.

fw-polyphony-history.title: The Silent Side of Polyphony: On the Disappearances of Silentium! from the Drafts of Dostoevskii and Bakhtin
fw-polyphony-history.notes: Historical distinction between 1929 Problems of Dostoevsky's Art and 1963 revised Problems of Dostoevsky's Poetics.

fw-polyphony-interpretation.title: Anatoly Korchinsky, The Politics of Polyphony: Dangerous Modernity and the Structure of the Novel in Dostoevsky and Bakhtin (2023 online)
fw-polyphony-interpretation.notes: Polyphony as an ethical, social, and narrative relation among independent centers of consciousness; avoid POV count shorthand.

fw-polyphony-circle.title: The Bakhtin Circle: Philosophy, Culture and Politics
fw-polyphony-circle.notes: Background on Bakhtin's revisions, dialogism, social speech, Dostoevsky and novelistic form.

fw-time-genette-handbook.title: Time, The Living Handbook of Narratology
fw-time-genette-handbook.notes: Account of Genette: order, duration, frequency; singulative, iterative, repetitive; publication and terminology.

fw-time-tuebingen.title: University of Tuebingen, Narrative Time: Core Concepts
fw-time-tuebingen.notes: Concise academic breakdown of order, duration and frequency; analepsis and prolepsis.

fw-time-egan.title: Jennifer Egan, A Visit from the Goon Squad (2010), publisher description
fw-time-egan.notes: 2010 ebook date and 2011 paperback; interlinked stories crossing years and genres.

fw-unreliable-booth.title: Wayne C. Booth, The Rhetoric of Fiction (1961), University of Chicago Press
fw-unreliable-booth.notes: Original edition 1961, influential distinction of reliable versus unreliable narrators and narrative distance.

fw-unreliable-narrator.title: Narrator, The Living Handbook of Narratology
fw-unreliable-narrator.notes: Careful distinctions among narrator, perspective, and the axes of reliability.

fw-language-achebe-ngugi-debate.title: English and/in Africa: Reflections on the Language Question, Afropolitanism, and Linguistic Orientation (2024)
fw-language-achebe-ngugi-debate.notes: Reassesses Achebe and Ngugi positions, historical context of 1962 conference, and continuing debate.

fw-language-anzaldua-translation.title: Karen Lorraine Cresci, How to Translate a Wild Tongue (2022)
fw-language-anzaldua-translation.notes: The multilingual form and translation difficulties of Anzaldua Borderlands/La Frontera (1987).

fw-language-anzaldua-bilingual.title: Marlene Hansen Esplin, Self-translation and Accommodation: Strategies of Multilingualism (2016)
fw-language-anzaldua-bilingual.notes: Scholarship on multilingual literary poetics in Anzaldua and Cota-Cardenas.

fw-language-venuti.title: Lawrence Venuti, The Translator's Invisibility: A History of Translation (1995), Library of Congress
fw-language-venuti.notes: Verified publication 1995 and discussion of fluency and translating cultural effects.

fw-ideas-murdoch-against.title: Iris Murdoch, Against Dryness (1961), annotated bibliographic entry
fw-ideas-murdoch-against.notes: Murdoch essay in Encounter January 1961, pages 16-20.

fw-ideas-murdoch-stanford.title: Iris Murdoch, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
fw-ideas-murdoch-stanford.notes: Moral attention, separateness of persons, Murdoch novels and philosophy; distinguishes scholarship from craft application.

fw-ideas-coetzee-animals.title: J. M. Coetzee, The Lives of Animals (1999), Princeton University Press
fw-ideas-coetzee-animals.notes: Fictional Elizabeth Costello lectures, family response and moral debate.

fw-ideas-coetzee-mulhall.title: Stephen Mulhall, The Wounded Animal (2009), Princeton University Press
fw-ideas-coetzee-mulhall.notes: Confirms Tanner Lectures 1997, The Lives of Animals 1999 and Elizabeth Costello 2003.

fw-ideas-leguin-dispossessed.title: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Dispossessed (1974), official author bibliography
fw-ideas-leguin-dispossessed.notes: First published 1974, imagined social institutions and contrasting forms of political organization.

fw-short-poe-review.title: Edgar Allan Poe, Review of Twice-Told Tales (Graham’s Magazine, May 1842)
fw-short-poe-review.notes: Text of Poe’s 1842 review used for his argument about the unity of effect in brief tales; a prescriptive position, not a universal rule.

fw-short-munro-nobel.title: Alice Munro, Nobel Lecture / In Her Own Words (2013)
fw-short-munro-nobel.notes: Pre-recorded interview shown in place of an in-person lecture; discusses reading, writing, revision, and hopes for readers.

fw-short-munro-bio.title: Alice Munro, Nobel Prize biographical account (2013/2014)
fw-short-munro-bio.notes: Archival discussion of drafts, revisions and the life-spanning scope of Munro’s short fiction.

fw-short-davis-interview.title: Lydia Davis, The Art of Fiction No. 227 (The Paris Review, 2015)
fw-short-davis-interview.notes: Interview on naming, compact forms, and compositional habits; no universal formula inferred.

fw-genre-slipstream-sfe.title: Slipstream SF, The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction
fw-genre-slipstream-sfe.notes: Explains the contested and shifting use of slipstream and its relationship to genre science fiction.

fw-genre-sterling-sfe.title: Bruce Sterling, The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction
fw-genre-sterling-sfe.notes: Documents Sterling’s 1989 discussion of slipstream and its emphasis on effect.

fw-genre-vandermeer-definition.title: Jeff VanderMeer, Working Definition of New Weird (2007)
fw-genre-vandermeer-definition.notes: Working genre definition by an involved editor; not an authoritative rule for all texts.

fw-genre-vandermeer-intro.title: Jeff VanderMeer, The New Weird Anthology: Notes and Introduction (2009)
fw-genre-vandermeer-intro.notes: Discusses the anthology published in 2008 and historical, disputed boundaries of the term.

fw-genre-kellylink.title: Kelly Link, Get in Trouble (2015)
fw-genre-kellylink.notes: Author site describing the 2015 story collection; quoted book descriptions should not be treated as universal genre theory.

fw-revision-saunders.title: George Saunders, A Swim in a Pond in the Rain (2021)
fw-revision-saunders.notes: Publication details and description of Saunders’s close-reading approach to short fiction.

fw-revision-mcphee-structure.title: John McPhee, Structure (The New Yorker, 2013)
fw-revision-mcphee-structure.notes: Nonfiction composition and arrangement; explicitly borrowed as a comparison rather than a claim about universal fiction process.

fw-revision-mcphee-draft4.title: John McPhee, Draft No. 4 (The New Yorker, 2013)
fw-revision-mcphee-draft4.notes: McPhee’s first-person account of drafts, reading aloud, and word-level revision in nonfiction.

fw-revision-salesses.title: Matthew Salesses, Craft in the Real World (2021)
fw-revision-salesses.notes: Challenges universalized workshop standards and examines author, audience and convention.

fw-cycle-ingram.title: Forrest L. Ingram, Representative Short Story Cycles of the Twentieth Century: Studies in a Literary Genre (1971)
fw-cycle-ingram.notes: Original Mouton edition; influential scholarly definition balancing autonomy of stories with coherence of the whole.

fw-cycle-strout.title: Elizabeth Strout, Olive Kitteridge (author page, originally 2008)
fw-cycle-strout.notes: Author describes thirteen interconnected narratives and their central recurring character.

fw-cycle-strout-pulitzer.title: 2009 Pulitzer Prize in Fiction: Elizabeth Strout, Olive Kitteridge
fw-cycle-strout-pulitzer.notes: Pulitzer calls it a collection of thirteen short stories.

fw-cycle-egan.title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize in Fiction: Jennifer Egan, A Visit from the Goon Squad
fw-cycle-egan.notes: Describes interlocking narratives; original book published in 2010.

fw-workshop-chavez.title: Felicia Rose Chavez, The Anti-Racist Writing Workshop (2021)
fw-workshop-chavez.notes: Author introduction and publication information for the pedagogy.

fw-workshop-lerman.title: Liz Lerman, Critical Response Process (official overview)
fw-workshop-lerman.notes: Describes origin in 1990, three roles, and four phases of responding to creative work.

fw-historical-mantel.title: Hilary Mantel, Can These Bones Live?, BBC Reith Lectures, Lecture 4 (2017)
fw-historical-mantel.notes: Fourth Reith lecture transcript. Includes BBC notice that its transcription may contain errors; paraphrase rather than rely on exact quotations.

fw-historical-hartman.title: Saidiya Hartman, Venus in Two Acts, Small Axe 12(2) (2008), pp. 1-14
fw-historical-hartman.notes: Archives of Atlantic slavery, critical fabulation, limits of reconstructing enslaved womens lives; not a generic license for fictive reconstruction.

fw-interactive-montfort.title: Nick Montfort, Twisty Little Passages: An Approach to Interactive Fiction (2003)
fw-interactive-montfort.notes: MIT Press page; first hardcover edition 2003, paperback 2005.

fw-interactive-twine.title: Twine: An Open-Source Tool for Telling Interactive, Nonlinear Stories
fw-interactive-twine.notes: Official description of linked passages, variables, conditional logic and HTML export.

fw-interactive-inform.title: Inform 7 official documentation: Writing with Inform and Recipe Book
fw-interactive-inform.notes: Inform 7 as a natural-language-based programming language for writing interactive fiction.

fw-interactive-inform-release.title: Nick Montfort, Announcing Inform 7 (April 30, 2006)
fw-interactive-inform-release.notes: Contemporary public release note, distinguishing Inform 7 from earlier Inform systems.
